sentences.text: This application has been preferred by the appellant for grant of bail to him during the pendency of this appeal.
The appellant has been convicted for the offence punishable u/s 376 of the Indian Penal Code and has been sentenced to undergo imprisonment for life along with a fine of Rs. 5,00,000/-.
It has been alleged that the appellant on the pretext of marriage had sexually exploited the informant as a result of which she had given birth to a child on 12.02.2016.
Subsequently once the appellant had got a service as a Gangman he had discontinued his relationship with the informant and also did not make any efforts to maintain her as well as her daughter.
Submission has been advanced by the learned Senior Counsel for the appellant that the occurrence is said to have taken place in 2011 and the First Information Report was lodged on 29.01.2019.
It has been submitted that the informant is aged 26 years and for 08 long years she had a physical relationship with the appellant but had never objected to the same.
Learned Senior Counsel submits that the appellant was all along on bail during trial.

sentences.text: Mr. Pankaj Kumar, learned P.P. has opposed the prayer for bail of the appellant.

Regard being had to the inordinate delay in instituting the case and the apparent consent on the part of the informant in establishing physical relationship with the appellant, we are inclined to admit the appellant on bail.

Accordingly, during the pendency of this appeal, the appellant is directed to be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand only) with two sureties of the like amount each, to the satisfaction of learned Additional Sessions Judge-II, Latehar in S.T. Case No.
162/2019, arising out of Latehar Mahila P.S. Case No. 02/2019.
I.A. No. 5098 of 2025 stands disposed of.

(Rongon Mukhopadhyay, J.) (Ambuj Nath, J.) A. Sanga/-
